audit.whatIsWrong: The full and content charts read Sett/Sett/Sett/Skill/Sett/Skill/Skill while this page's own whys[] text said the opposite on four rows ('Level 1 is Garen's', 'Level 2 stays Garen', 'Levels 4-5 stay yours', 'First item swings back to Garen'). The mirror (garen__sett) settled the chart as Garen/Garen/Sett/Sett/Sett/Garen/Skill.
audit.why: The side tokens contradicted the prose sitting directly beside them, and contradicted the mirror. The packet agrees on rows 0-5 (Garen, Garen, Sett, Sett, Sett, Garen); it reads Sett on row 6 where the mirror settled Skill, so I followed the mirror rather than reopen a decided row.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 1, 3 and 5 flipped in both layers as one atomic group with ratings moved to match, phase whys rewritten to the new owners, and whys[6] de-claimed so it no longer says the late game 'returns to you' on a Skill row.

audit.whatIsWrong: The first-item spike said only 'respect his trade windows' — no cooldown, no named window, and no mention of the thing that actually eats the burst.
audit.why: Courage is 22/19.5/17/14.5/12s and gives a shield plus tenacity on cast; it is the exact cooldown that decides whether an all-in works. Facebreaker is 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s and Haymaker 18/16.5/15/13.5/12s.
audit.corrected: Courage's 12s at rank 5 keyed to the first-item and late text, Facebreaker's 13s to the mid-lane instruction.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three interaction errors. (a) Facebreaker was written as a stun in every line — it only stuns when enemies are on opposite sides of Sett, so a lone Garen takes a slow. (b) Decisive Strike explicitly 'break[s] free of all slows', so that slow is purged the instant he casts it — the page never said so. (c) The Show Stopper was credited with true damage; the true damage is Haymaker's centre.
audit.why: Riot's Sett E text: 'If enemies were only on one side, they are slowed instead of stunned.' Riot's Garen Q text: 'gains a burst of Move Speed, breaking free of all slows affecting him.' Riot's Sett W text puts true damage in the centre and physical on the sides; the R text has no true-damage clause at all. The mirror recorded the same three corrections, so both sides now match.
audit.corrected: Spike, mid and late text now tell the player to line Garen up against the wave so Facebreaker stuns rather than slows, warn that Decisive Strike purges the one-sided slow, and move the true-damage credit onto Haymaker's centre.

audit.whatIsWrong: Both applicable missing interactions were absent: Courage absorbs the burst window, and Decisive Strike opens with an auto-attack reset.
audit.why: The reset means the tell is the wind-up animation, not the ability cast — a player watching for the cast has already taken the hit. And committing a max-Grit Haymaker into a fresh Courage wastes the one window the lane gives you.
audit.corrected: Auto-reset tell added to the level-1 and early text; the force-Courage-first rule added to the first-item spike and the late text.

edits.before: Double-punch passive makes you the strongest level-1 auto-trader in the lane. Punish Garen on every CS, but respect his opening tool — chips now, all-ins later.
edits.after: Decisive Strike is an auto reset that silences, so his wind-up is your cue to step back, not the cast. Take the level-1 loss, chip on last-hits, wait for Facebreaker.

edits.before: Q gives move speed toward Garen and two empowered punches. Take short Q trades and back off before he can answer with Courage.
edits.after: Judgment out-damages your dry walk-up at 2, and Decisive Strike purges the slow off a one-sided E. Take the chip, bank Grit, and wait.

edits.before: Q ranks make your punch trades heavier, but Garen has his core tools too. Keep the grit bar honest: trade in, W-shield his return damage, out.
edits.after: Q ranks make your punch trades heavier and Facebreaker (13s) pins him through Judgment. Trade in, cash W with him dead-centre, then step out.

edits.before: Stridebreaker fixes your only weakness — sticking to Garen. Shove, recall on the spike, and force the next trade before he matches your item.
edits.after: Garen spikes harder on his first bruiser item: Courage is 12s at rank 5 and its shield eats your burst, so force it out before you commit to anything.

edits.before: Sterak's makes your all-in nearly unburstable. Fights are decided by whether you cash a max-grit W — track Courage and commit on the gap.
edits.after: Sterak's makes your all-in nearly unburstable. Duels come down to whether Courage is down and whether Haymaker lands with Garen dead-centre.

edits.before: 2+ items returns to you as Grit and R-cancel win isolated duels.
edits.after: 2+ items is a coin-flip decided by whether Courage is down.

edits.before: The lane swings to you here — once you have E Facebreaker plus Q you can lock Garen in place, so when he Q Decisive Strike silences and runs at you, E-pull and W Haymaker the stored damage before his passive regen resets his health.
edits.after: The lane swings to you at 3, but Facebreaker only stuns with a minion opposite him — pull a lone Garen and he takes a slow that Decisive Strike purges outright. Line him up against your wave, then cash Haymaker before Perseverance ticks his health back.

edits.before: Your R The Show Stopper suppress denies Garen's R Demacian Justice execute and slams him for true damage; at 6 you hold the all-in as long as you dodge or tank his E Judgment spin on Grit.
edits.after: Your R The Show Stopper suppress denies Garen's R Demacian Justice execute; the true damage is Haymaker's centre, so land him mid-panel. Tank Judgment on Grit and the all-in is yours.

edits.before: Garen spikes back on early bruiser items — his Q silence plus E spin shreds you if you fight into it dry, so respect his trade windows and only commit when your E and W are up to interrupt his spin.
edits.after: Garen spikes back on early bruiser items — Q silence into Judgment shreds a dry fight. Force Courage out first: it is 12s at rank 5, and its shield plus tenacity eats exactly the burst window you were counting on.

edits.before: With built Grit and R to cancel Demacian Justice you reclaim the edge in an isolated duel — bait his Q silence, tank the E spin, then E-Haymaker him once his passive and Q are on cooldown.
edits.after: Isolated duels come down to Courage — bait it out, tank Judgment on Grit, then line Garen up against a minion so Facebreaker stuns instead of slowing, and cash Haymaker on his centre.

edits.before: Levels 1-2 are Garen's — his Q Decisive Strike silence-and-move lets him force a trade and then walk off to regen with passive before you can answer, and his E spin out-damages your dry walk-up.
edits.after: Levels 1-2 are Garen's — Decisive Strike is an auto reset, so his wind-up is your cue to step back, not the cast. He trades, walks off, and Perseverance refunds it before you can answer.

edits.before: From level 3 the lane tips to you: E Facebreaker pins Garen so he can't kite out after his Q, and your E-Q-W trade plus level-6 R suppress (which denies his Demacian Justice) win the all-in as long as you handle his spin on Grit.
edits.after: From level 3 the lane tips to you, but Facebreaker (13s) only stuns with a target on each side — pull Garen against your wave or he takes a slow that Decisive Strike purges. Then Q-W with him centred.

edits.before: Garen spikes again on his first bruiser item where his Q-silence-into-E burst punishes a dry fight, but into 2+ items your built Grit and R-cancel let you reclaim isolated duels — bait the silence, tank the spin, then Haymaker him on his cooldowns.
edits.after: Garen spikes again on his first bruiser item, where Q-silence into Judgment punishes a dry fight. Into 2+ items it is decided by Courage (12s): force the shield and its tenacity out first, tank the spin, then Haymaker him dead-centre on his cooldowns.
